description: *** 27 August 2026 - Amendment W9127N26BA0240001 Bonneville Lock and Dam - Navigation Lock 1 Bridge Replacement*** This amendment inserts additional Government Furnished Information (GFI) as an attachment to the solicitation. The file �Power Line Layout� is provided for the Contractor�s information. Information provided should be field verified by the Contractor. If there is a discrepancy between the solicitation plan set and the GFI, the solicitation plan set takes precedence. The project consists of replacing the existing bridge with a new fixed bridge on a new alignment and to provide for partial demolition of the existing bridge. The new fixed bridge will be a single-span steel girder bridge with a concrete deck. The bridge width will be 34�4�� out-to-out, with two 11�0� travel lanes, two 2�0� shoulders, a 5�0� sidewalk, and the superstructure will consist of four (4) built-up steel plate girders. The replacement bridge alignment is located immediately downstream of the existing bridge and, at its northern terminus, will fit entirely between the existing bridge and the Bonneville Power Administration transmission tower which is located to the south. Approach roadways will also be constructed to tie into the existing roadway alignment. The new fixed bridge will be located over the existing navigation channel and will provide an under clearance that is larger than is currently present under the existing bridge. The north abutment will be a concrete stub abutment with spread footing anchored into rock. The south abutment will be a concrete abutment that is supported by drilled shafts. To mitigate seismic hazards, portions of the existing bridge will be removed as part of the bridge construction requirement. The existing bridge provides for critical vehicular access to the Bonneville project that must remain open for the entirety of the construction project. This will likely require the contractor to construct the project in phases. In addition, lead and asbestos removal will be required as part of this requirement. description: The US Army Corps of Engineers, Walla Walla District is seeking small business sources for HVAC Troubleshooting, Repair, and Maintenance Services (Blanket Purchase Agreement). The work is located within USACE Walla Walla District to include work in Idaho, Oregon, and Washington. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this project is 238220, Plumbing, Heating and Air-Conditioning Contractors, and the associated small business size standard is no more than $19,000,000 in average annual receipts. This sources-sought announcement is a tool to identify businesses with the capability to accomplish the work. This is not a solicitation. Further information regarding this project will be available through SAM.gov upon release of the solicitation. The solicitation will include sustainability clauses as appropriate for the project. Only those firms who respond to this announcement by submitting the following information will be used in determining whether to set aside this requirement. All interested offerors are required to provide the following: A list of current or past projects demonstrating technical experience with work of a similar nature to that listed in the Summary Scope of Work. For each project submitted, provide a brief narrative statement of the work involved, your firm's role in the project, the dollar value, and the completion date. Include a statement detailing any special qualifications and certifications applicable to the scope of this project, held by your firm and/or in-house personnel. A reference list for each of the projects submitted in 1) above. Include the name, title, phone number, and email address for each reference. A statement of your firm's business size (Small Business, HUBZone Small Business, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business, 8(a), Small Disadvantaged Business, or Women-Owned Small Business) with regard to the NAICS code listed above. A statement that your firm intends to submit an offer on the project when it is advertised. Your firm's CAGE Code and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI). Confirmation that your firm can comply with FAR 52.219-14 (Limitations on Subcontracting) by performing at least 50 percent of the cost of contract performance incurred for personnel with its own employees or similarly situated entities. Answers to the following questions: a. Given the wide variance in equipment in the scope (from wall-mounted PTACs to 1,500-ton industrial water-sourced heat pumps), what is your firm's core competency? For which systems do you primarily rely on in-house technicians versus sub-contractors? b. Do your in-house technicians hold specific OEM (Original Equipment Manufacturer) factory certifications for large-tonnage industrial systems (e.g., Trane, Carrier, York, Daikin)? If so, please list them. c. When utilizing sub-contractors for specialized or heavy industrial HVAC repairs, how do you vet their qualifications, safety compliance, and workmanship? d. For critical industrial HVAC failures, what is your standard emergency response time for having a qualified technician on-site? e. How do you manage your supply chain and parts sourcing to minimize downtime for legacy or highly specialized HVAC equipment? f. For a Blanket Purchase Agreement of this nature, what pricing structures are most standard and efficient for your firm (e.g., fully loaded hourly rates for different technician labor categories, standard markups on parts/materials, flat rates for preventative maintenance)? g. Are there any industry standards, commercial practices, or specific terms and conditions we should consider including in this BPA to make it more attractive to highly qualified vendors? Submit this information to Hillary Morgan, Contracting Officer, via email to hillary.a.morgan@usace.army.mil. Your response to this notice must be received on or before 4:00 PM on Friday, 18 September 2026. SUMMARY OF SCOPE OF WORK: HVAC Troubleshooting, Repair, and Maintenance Services (Blanket Purchase Agreement) GENERAL OBJECTIVE The purpose of this Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) is to establish agreement terms for providing comprehensive troubleshooting, repair, and preventative maintenance services for various heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems. SCOPE OF SERVICES The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal services necessary to perform troubleshooting, repair, and maintenance on HVAC systems as defined in individual call orders. All work shall be performed in accordance with industry standards, manufacturer specifications, and applicable local, state, and federal regulations (including OSHA safety standards). EQUIPMENT COVERED The scope of work applies to, but is not limited to, the following types of HVAC equipment and systems: Heat Pumps (Standard): Residential and commercial heat pump systems with capacities up to 10 tons (120,000 BTU/hr). Large Water-Sourced Heat Pumps: Industrial facility water-sourced heat pump systems with capacities of up to 1,500 tons. Split Systems: Both ducted and ductless split-type HVAC units. Mini-Splits: Ductless mini-split systems of various capacities. Roof-Mounted Packaged Units: Commercial packaged heating and cooling units located on rooftops. Packaged Terminal Air Conditioners (PTAC): Hotel room-style wall-mounted units. DESCRIPTION OF TASKS Troubleshooting & Diagnostics: Identify the root cause of equipment failures or performance degradation. Provide a detailed diagnostic report and repair estimate prior to commencing repair work. Repair Services: Perform authorized repairs to restore equipment to full operational status in accordance with the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) specifications. This includes repairing or replacing defective components, recharging refrigerants, and fixing electrical connections. Preventative Maintenance: Conduct routine maintenance tasks such as cleaning coils, replacing filters, checking refrigerant levels, lubricating moving parts, inspecting electrical components, and verifying thermostat operations to ensure optimal system efficiency and longevity. PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS Qualified Personnel: All technicians performing work under this BPA must be properly licensed and certified (e.g., EPA Section 608 certification for refrigerant handling) to work on the specified equipment. Teaming and Subcontracting: The prime Contractor is responsible for assembling the required expertise for each job. As required by the complexity or specific technical needs of the equipment, the Contractor shall team up with the appropriate, specialized sub-contractors needed to successfully service the units identified in any individual BPA call order. Workmanship: All repairs and maintenance shall be completed to a professional standard, leaving the work area clean and free of debris upon completion. Reporting: The Contractor shall provide written service reports for each visit detailing the equipment serviced, issues found, actions taken, parts replaced, and recommendations for future maintenance.

title: 37250PR260000050 - USCG AIR STATION SAN DIEGO CREW BERTHING ROOMS RENOVATIONS - CONSTRUCTION
description: Solicitation: Aircrew Duty Berthing Renovations Set-Aside: Total Small Business Set-Aside (FAR Subpart 19.5) Location: USCG Sector San Diego, Building D (Aircrew Duty Berthing Room), 2170 N. Harbor Drive, San Diego, CA 92101 Important Dates Questions Due: September 15, 2026 Proposals Due: September 18, 2026, by 11:59 PM Eastern Time 1. Project Background and Objective The U.S. Coast Guard requires complete renovations of the Aircrew Duty Berthing Room in Building D at Sector San Diego. The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, transportation, tools, materials, and supervision necessary to modernize the space for active-duty personnel. 2. Scope of Work (Summary) - Please review the attached Statement of Work (SOW) for full technical requirements, safety standards, and applicable codes. The Contractor is responsible for the demolition of existing materials and the installation of new commercial-grade fixtures. Key tasks include: Lighting Renovation: Replace existing light fixtures with new fully dimmable LED fixtures featuring a selectable red-light mode across 6 sleeping rooms, 1 central hallway, and 1 bathroom. Bathroom Renovation: Demolish existing fixtures, tile, and shower pan. Install a new commercial-grade toilet, sink/vanity with enclosed storage, shower pan, low-maintenance sheet vinyl flooring, and a new mirror. Flooring Installation: Remove approximately 590 sq ft of existing carpet and install new Luxury Vinyl Plank (LVP) flooring, including new baseboards and trim. Interior Painting: Prepare and paint all interior walls and trim in the 6 sleeping rooms and the common passageway. 3. Site Conditions & Hazardous Materials An Asbestos and Lead Survey was conducted for this facility (AESS Job No. 26-092). Asbestos: No asbestos was detected in the Berthing Room in Building D. Lead: Lead was detected at very low concentrations (<0.00146% to 0.0039% by weight). While below the EPA/HUD threshold for Lead-Based Paint, any detectable level of lead triggers Cal/OSHA Lead in Construction Standard (8 CCR � 1532.1) compliance. Handling & Disposal: Debris and waste generated from the removal of lead-containing materials must be evaluated for appropriate disposal classification (TCLP or TTLC) prior to off-site disposal. Government dumpsters shall not be used. 4. Period of Performance and Hours All work shall be completed within 60 calendar days from the issuance of the written Notice to Proceed (NTP). Work hours are Monday through Friday, 0800 to 1700 hours, excluding federal holidays. Any disruption to utilities must be coordinated at least 72 hours in advance. 5. Wage Determinations This project is subject to the Davis-Bacon Act (FAR 52.222-6). Prevailing wages for San Diego County, CA, apply. See the attached General Decision Wage Determination. 6. Proposal Submission Requirements To be considered for award, interested offerors must submit the following documents with their proposal: Product Data Sheets & Warranties: For LED lighting fixtures, bathroom vanity, toilet, shower pan, LVP flooring, and any other major items to be replaced. Samples: Paint color and flooring finish samples or spec sheets. Safety Plans: An Activity Hazard Analysis (AHA) & Accident Prevention Plan (APP) detailing Cal/OSHA compliance for lead-containing materials and general construction safety. Technical Plan: Detailed technical plan outlining the project schedule from the post-award walk-through to construction completion. Past Performance & Licensing: Relevant past performance examples and proof of valid professional and trade licenses (plumbing, electrical, tile-setting). Pricing: Transparent pricing sheet breaking down labor, materials, waste disposal, and the total proposed cost. Attachments Statement of Work (SOW) - Aircrew Duty Berthing Renovations Davis-Bacon Wage Determination - San Diego, CA Asbestos and Lead Survey Report - AESS Job No. 26-092 All questions should be directed to the Contracting Officer prior to the Q&A deadline.

title: Germany – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Forschungsprojekt - DZSF - Erstellung eines Katalogs mit Anpassungsmaßnahmen gegen klimabedingte Einwirkungen auf die Verkehrsinfrastruktur
description: Extremwetterereignisse und der Klimawandel stellen Verkehrssysteme weltweit bereits heute vor bedeutende Herausforderungen. Mit voranschreitendem Klimawandel ist davon auszugehen, dass extreme Wetterereignisse in Zukunft häufiger auftreten werden und somit potentiell auch größere Schäden verursachen können. Eine Anpassung der Verkehrsinfrastruktur an den Klimawandel ist daher eine notwendige Bedingung, damit das Transportsystem auch unter zukünftigen klimatischen Bedingungen leistungsfähig und verlässlich bleibt. In diesem Zusammenhang soll ein Katalog mit Anpassungsmaßnahmen entwickelt werden, der eine fundierte Grundlage bildet, die sowohl für Fallstudien von entwickelten Maßnahmen als auch für die zukünftige Maßnahmenpriorisierung, -auswahl und -umsetzung in der Praxis genutzt werden kann. In einem ersten Schritt werden Informationen zu verkehrsträgerübergreifenden Hotspots (KV-Terminals und Bereiche, in denen mehrere Verkehrsträger räumlich nah beieinander liegen) im deutschen Verkehrsnetz zusammengetragen. Darauf aufbauend werden im zweiten Schritt bereits umgesetzte Anpassungsmaßnahmen an den Hotspots recherchiert und um weitere mögliche Anpassungsmaßnahmen ergänzt und bewertet. Abschließend werden die Anpassungsoptionen in einem Katalog zusammengefasst, kategorisiert und bewertet.

description: Advance Procurement Notice DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION OF THE SNOW AND ICE CONTROL (SNIC) HEAVY EQUIPMENT (HE) FACILITY (MODIFIED DESIGN-BUILD) COLD LAKE, ALBERTA (with Security Requirements) Purpose of this Advance Procurement Notice This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals. In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform Design Builders of an upcoming contract opportunity at 4 Wing Cold Lake, Alberta. The purpose of this APN is to allow Design Builders to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process, notably by initiating any necessary steps. This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested Design Builders to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable). Please note that this project may include an Indigenous businesses participation component in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process. Description of the Project and Services The delivery method for this project will be Modified Design-Build (MDB). The Defence of Canada Fighter Infrastructure (DCFI) project was identified as part of the Continental Defence Memorandum to Cabinet. DCFI intends to modernize, recapitalize, and add new critical infrastructure, including Information Management/Information Technology (IM/IT) upgrades, to enable Canada’s ability to project air power in defence of North America for the coming decades. The purpose of DCFI is to build upon and complement the infrastructure work under the Future Fighter Capability Project (FFCP). The Snow and Ice Control (SNIC)/Heavy Equipment (HE) Facility project at 4 Wing Cold Lake, Alberta is a major infrastructure initiative under DCFI. It involves constructing a new, purpose-built facility to consolidate all SNIC and HE operations, storage, and maintenance in one facility with direct airfield access. The facility will support year-round airfield operations for NORAD, search and rescue, and future fighter missions, including the CF-35A. title: Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) Frequency Reference System (FRS) Flight
description: NASA/GSFC has a requirement for the design, fabrication, qualification, and delivery of flight Frequency Reference System (FRS) hardware for NASA's Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) mission, consisting of three Flight Models and one Flight Spare. Each FRS unit comprises two tightly coupled subsystems, the FRS optical reference cavity (FRS-O) and the FRS frequency-locking electronics (FRS-E), which together stabilize the laser frequency using a Pound-Drever-Hall lock to meet LISA's picometer-scale measurement needs, with deliveries required on an aggressive schedule between February 2029 and May 2030. Minimal post-delivery support is included. NASA/GSFC intends to issue a sole source contract to BAE Systems Space & Mission Systems Inc. (BAE SMS) under the authority of FAR 6.103-1, to acquire the LISA FRS flight hardware. Based on a publicly issued Sources Sought Notice, only BAE SMS is capable of meeting the full FRS-O and FRS-E requirements within the fixed delivery schedule. BAE SMS possesses directly relevant flight heritage across both the FRS-O and FRS-E subsystems, including the GRACE Follow-On and GRACE-C optical cavities that are heritage to the LISA FRS-O, and it is already under contract with NASA GSFC developing mature, pre-flight LISA FRS hardware through a full Technology Readiness Level and Engineering Test Unit phase. This existing hardware baseline, combined with BAE's established relationships with the specialized suppliers of the custom, long-lead FRS components, positions BAE SMS to meet the aggressive delivery dates required for NASA system-level integration and subsequent delivery to ESA under the NASA-ESA Memorandum of Understanding. No other source possesses the hardware maturity, technical heritage, or supplier relationships to successfully meet NASA requirements. Accordingly, only one responsible source can satisfy the Government's requirements, and no other supplies or services will meet the agency's need. The Government does not intend to acquire a commercial product or commercial service using FAR Part 12. Interested organizations may submit their capabilities and qualifications to perform the effort electronically via email to stefan.d.flessa@nasa.gov not later than 4:30 PM Eastern Time on September 19, 2026. Such capabilities/qualifications will be evaluated solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct this acquisition on a competitive basis. A decision by the Government not to compete this acquisition on a full and open competition basis, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government. title: Germany – Single-purpose sports facilities construction work – Sanierung Hallenbad Weikersheim_2.BA_Edelstahlschwimmbecken
description: Gewerk: Edelstahlschwimmbecken - Stahlbauarbeiten Die Stadt Weikersheim beabsichtigt die umfassende Sanierung des bestehenden Hallenbades, das baulich in den Schulkomplex des Gymnasiums integriert ist. Die Sanierung des Lehrschwimmbeckens erfolgt im Rahmen einer Gesamtmaßnahme in zwei Bauabschnitten. Gegenstand der vorliegenden Ausschreibung ist die Erneuerung des bestehenden Lehrschwimmbeckens durch ein Edelstahlbecken einschließlich der hierfür erforderlichen Rohbau- und Anschlussarbeiten. Das bestehende, geflieste Betonbecken mit einer Größe von ca. 20,00 × 8,00 m wird vollständig zurückgebaut bzw. für die Aufnahme des neuen Edelstahlbeckens entsprechend vorbereitet. Das neue Becken ist einschließlich aller erforderlichen konstruktiven und technischen Anschlüsse fachgerecht herzustellen und zu montieren. Der ausgeschriebene Leistungsumfang umfasst insbesondere die Werk- und Montageplanung, Produktion, Lieferung und Endmontage des Edelstahlbeckens sowie die unmittelbar am Beckenkörper erforderlichen Rohbauarbeiten. Hierzu gehören unter anderem die Auffüllung der Technikebene im Bereich des Beckenbodens, Ortbetonarbeiten an den Bodeneinströmkanälen, Arbeiten an den Rinnenköpfen sowie die Ausbildung und Anpassung der Übergänge zwischen Boden- und Wandblechen. Die Leistungen sind im Bestand und unter Berücksichtigung der vorhandenen baulichen Gegebenheiten des Hallenbades auszuführen. Sämtliche für die vollständige, funktionsgerechte und fachgerechte Herstellung des neuen Edelstahlbeckens erforderlichen Neben- und Anschlussarbeiten sind Bestandteil der Leistung, soweit sie in den Vergabeunterlagen beschrieben sind. Die Ausführung der Komplettsanierung des Lehrschwimmbeckens ist für den Zeitraum von November 2026 bis August 2027 vorgesehen.

Valtion ja Tampereen kaupunkiseudun välisessä MAL sopimuksessa vuosille 2024–2027 on sovittu Epilän ja Harjuniityn seisakkeiden suunnittelusta. Seisakkeet sijaitsevat hankealueella ja sisältyvät optiona suunnittelukokonaisuuteen. Lisäraiteesta on laadittu aluevaraussuunnitelma vuonna 2015 osana laajempaa kokonaisuutta Tampere-Lielahti-Nokia/Ylöjärvi. Vuonna 2020 valmistuneessa Tampere-Pori tarveselvityksessä on hanke esitetty kolmanneksi tärkeimmäksi kehittämistoimenpiteeksi etenkin, jos lähijunaliikenne seudulla kasvaa. Tärkeimmiksi tunnistetut kehittämistoimet on toteutettu rataosalla jo aiemmin. Tarveselvityksen jälkeen on rataosuudella lisätty ostoliikenteen lähijunavuoroja Nokialle. Tesoman seisake on valmistunut vuonna 2021 ja Nokian liikennepaikan kehittämistyöt vuonna 2025. Rauman seisakkeen rakennustyöt ovat käynnissä ja lisävuorot Raumalta Tampereelle on käynnistymässä vuonna 2027. Epilän seisakkeen esiselvitys valmistuu keväällä 2026. Harjuniityn seisakkeen esiselvitys on laadittu aiemmin kaavatyön yhteydessä. Tesoman seisakkeen vaiheittainen toteutus ja lisäraide on huomioitu seisakkeen lainvoimaisessa ratasuunnitelmassa (4.9.2020). Nokian liikennepaikan kehittämisen yhteydessä on selvitetty lisäraiteen sijoittuminen liikennepaikan kohdalla ja tältä osin aluevaraussuunnitelmaa on päivitetty vuonna 2021 julkaistussa liikennepaikan esiselvityksessä. Tampereen ja Nokian yleiskaavoissa lisäraidetarpeet on huomioitu kaavatyön yhteydessä. Asemakaavoissa lisäraidetarpeet on huomioitu varauksina niiltä osin, missä kaavamuutoksia on maankäytön kehittymisen seurauksena ollut tarve päivittää. Nokialla kuntarajalla, Kankaantakana ja Haavistossa on yhteensä n. 1 km hankealuetta asemakaavoittamatta. Palveluntuottajaksi valitaan yksi toimittaja. Hankinnan sisältö on määritelty tarkemmin tarjouspyyntöasiakirjoissa.
